notesStmt.note: A note on another of the several corrected proof slips of this poem (loc.02393) suggests that Whitman sent a copy of this poem for printing to the offices of The Century in June 1889. The note on the present manuscript suggests that this proof was sent to The Century after that, but before the publication in February 1890, as the version of the poem in the magazine includes the changes on this proof slip. The later printings of this poem in Good-Bye My Fancy and Leaves of Grass do not include these changes.

This is a proof slip of "Old Age's Ship and Crafty Death's," with corrections and notations in Whitman's hand. The poem was first published in the February 1890 issue of The Century Magazine. Whitman subsequently included it in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891) and in the printing of Leaves of Grass that he oversaw just before his death.

lg.head: OLD AGE'S SHIP & CRAFTY DEATH'S.
lg.l: FInitialrom east and west across the horizon's edge,
Two mighty masterful vessels, sailers, steal upon us:

But we'll make race a-time upon the seas—a battle-contest
yet! bear lively there!
(Our joys of strife and derring-do to the last!)
Put on the old ship all her power to-day!

Out challenge and defiance—flags and flaunting pennants
added,
As we take to the open—take to the deepest, freest waters.
